note: An AI coding assistant, such as Claude Code or Codex, that reads, writes, and runs code for you.
A folder of instructions an agent loads when a task needs it, such as how to open a pull request.
Which model and effort agents use for each kind of work, such as a fast model for lookups and a strong one for reviews.
An app that runs agent threads on your machines and shows them on every device.
One agent conversation in T3 Code, with its own task, often in its own worktree.
A separate checkout of the same repo, so several threads can change code at once without touching each other.
A Linux machine, local or in the cloud, where agents and threads run.
A devbox that stays on overnight, so scheduled agent work can run while you sleep.
One always-on devbox that manages your other machines: it shares your MCP servers, keeps your devboxes linked, and watches their disks. Only the Hub pack adds one.
A connector that gives agents a tool, such as Slack or your analytics, through the Model Context Protocol.
A plan for big work: one issue that lists tickets, each small enough for one pull request.
The thread that works through a map. It starts one worker thread for each ticket that is ready.
A pull request that is not yet ready for review. Agents open drafts, and you decide when one is ready.
Evidence beside each behavior a pull request changes: a test that failed before and passes after, or output from the real system.
A phrase you type to tell the agent to take this pull request to merged and rolled out, without asking again.
A phrase you type to tell the agent to get this pull request an approving review, then merge it.
A platform for cloud development machines. Fleet uses its private port links for previews.
PostHog's developer CLI, which sets up and runs a PostHog devbox.
PostHog's bot that approves low-risk pull requests on request.
PostHog's AI review bot for pull requests.
